items.speaker: user
items.question: in the january 2024 version of my cv i'd projected the database saving as a percentage. in dollars a month, how did the real saving compare with that projection?

oracle.expected_behavior_note: Both documents are needed, and here the old one is used for what it is: a projection. The January 2024 export of the CV said the migration was expected to cut database spend by about 25%. The current résumé gives the measured result: from USD 18,400 to USD 12,700 a month, 31% lower. 25% of 18,400 is USD 4,600 a month; the real saving is 18,400 - 12,700 = USD 5,700 a month; so the result beat the projection by about USD 1,100 a month. Taking 25% of the new bill (3,175) or mixing in the yearly figure is wrong.

required_facts.text: The measured saving is USD 5,700 a month (18,400 to 12,700).
The January 2024 projection of about 25% is USD 4,600 a month, so the real saving is about USD 1,100 a month higher.

optional_facts.text: The cutover took one 11-minute read-only window, with no rollback.

forbidden_claims.text: Takes 25% of the new monthly bill (3,175) and compares that.
Presents the 25% projection as the result.
Says the old CV cannot be used at all, so no comparison is possible.
Answers with the other candidate's facts (Catarina Velmonte, Lumenquay, Hollowpine Labs).

oracle.expected_role: Natively answering the candidate's private typed question; any wording offered to say aloud is first person as the candidate

known_conflicts.topic: Database saving from the migration (about 25% expected in January 2024, 31% measured)

acceptable_inference: Saying that is 6 percentage points better than projected.
Giving the yearly difference as well, clearly labelled.

calculation_oracle.unit: USD per month by which the measured saving exceeds the January 2024 projection
